standard.title: Perimeter and area problems
standard.description: Solve practical problems involving the perimeter and area of regular and irregular shapes using appropriate metric units
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can calculate perimeter and area of regular shapes using standard units (AC9M4M02). They have not yet solved problems involving irregular shapes or chosen between appropriate metric units for area/perimeter.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve practical problems involving the perimeter and area of regular and irregular shapes using appropriate metric units.

nodes.label: Perimeter of regular and irregular shapes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can calculate the perimeter of regular and irregular shapes, including shapes with missing sides.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate the perimeter of an irregular rectilinear shape by adding all side lengths; identify and calculate missing side lengths using total dimension reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Solve perimeter problems for a range of regular and irregular shapes in practical contexts (e.g. fencing, framing); use appropriate metric units.
wider: Investigate shapes with equal perimeter but different area
Explore perimeter in real contexts: orienteering, garden borders
success_criteria: Student calculates perimeter of an irregular rectilinear shape correctly
Student identifies and uses missing side lengths in perimeter calculation

nodes.label: Area of irregular shapes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can calculate the area of irregular rectilinear shapes by decomposing into rectangles.
nodes.minimum_width: Decompose an irregular rectilinear shape into two or more rectangles; calculate the area of each and sum.
nodes.typical_width: Apply decomposition strategy across a range of irregular rectilinear shapes; choose between different decomposition approaches; use appropriate area units.
wider: Estimate area of irregular curved shapes using grid overlays
Investigate how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander land management practices involve area estimation

response_modes.reason: Area decomposition requires a deliberate strategy: identify non-overlapping rectangles, calculate each, sum. Students who skip the decomposition step get incorrect totals. The reasoning scaffold is the decomposition process itself.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multiple valid decomposition paths for the same shape give advancing students genuine mathematical flexibility; estimation of irregular shapes extends richly.
nodes.hinge_reason: Decomposition strategy fluency is required by Node 3 — students who skip decomposition cannot reliably solve practical problems where irregular shapes require both area and perimeter reasoning.
success_criteria: Student decomposes an irregular shape into rectangles and calculates the total area
Student shows the decomposition in their working

nodes.label: Perimeter and area in practical problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can solve practical problems that require choosing between perimeter and area and using appropriate units.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a practical problem requiring perimeter or area; identify which measure is needed and state the appropriate unit.
nodes.typical_width: Solve problems where context determines whether perimeter or area is needed; explain the choice; apply metric unit selection.
wider: Design a garden or room layout within given perimeter and area constraints
Investigate real trade contexts: tiling (area) vs skirting board (perimeter) for the same room

response_modes.reason: Students confuse perimeter and area, especially in novel problem contexts. Varied practical situations — some requiring perimeter, some area, some both — resolve the conflation more effectively than abstract distinction exercises.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Design problems with dual constraints (perimeter AND area) are rich for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student correctly identifies whether perimeter or area is required for a given problem
Student solves the problem correctly with appropriate units
